Donald Trump has downplayed a visit to Moscow by the CIA director, John Ratcliffe, as “semi-routine” after he turned up in the Russian capital unannounced, triggering a wave of speculation about the reasons for his trip.

Ratcliffe was reported to have flown to Moscow on a government transport plane on Tuesday in a rare visit after taking off from the Andrews air force base in Maryland.

events.summary:
Efforts to rebuild domestic food production face severe challenges and have come at deadly cost

As Gaza’s population of 2.1 million has been hemmed into an ever smaller slice of the territory, farmers are using every last remaining patch of unspoiled earth, no matter how tiny, in their struggle to survive.

With severe shortages of water, fertiliser and pesticide, and with more than 80% of greenhouses ruined, it has taken inventiveness and determination to clear land of debris and coax new seedlings into life. Moreover, venturing out into the open to tend to plants can be deadly.

events.summary:

Iran has taken the first step towards criminalising contact with foreign media, in a move human rights groups have said attempts to “sever the entire Iranian society from the rest of the world”.

For journalists, researchers and even ordinary citizens, the proposed law being discussed by Iranian lawmakers this month could make speaking to international audiences and groups a potential criminal act and restrict coverage of events such as January’s mass anti-regime protests.

events.summary:
Internal calls to end war get louder as Gulf neighbours plan alternative pipelines to cut reliance on waterway

Is the strait of Hormuz, recently cited by the office of the Iranian supreme leader as “the pillar of Iran’s new security order”, and as transformative as possessing a nuclear weapon, in reality becoming a fast-diminishing asset, leaving Iran increasingly vulnerable to the new planned US wave of economic sanctions?

It is the key debate that is raging inside Iran, with many different conclusions being drawn for Tehran’s negotiating strategy. Those who warn the strait’s value as a chokehold on the world economy will erode, leaving the country without foreign exchange reserves, argue that Iran’s negotiators should seek a deal soon.

China has denounced the threat of US sanctions for its trade with Iran, saying any such measures would be illegal, and warned it would take “all necessary measures” to protect its national interests.

Beijing’s rejection of the US threat of secondary sanctions for any country or entity continuing to trade with Tehran had been predicted. China buys an estimated 80% of Iran’s oil exports and has defied previous US efforts to limit the flow of revenue to the Tehran regime.

The international community was scrambling to get aid into flood-stricken parts of Nepal and Tibet on Thursday as authorities warned that a lake ⁠formed at the ⁠site ⁠where the ​deadly torrents occurred ⁠was rising and ⁠at risk ​of ‌bursting.

The devastating flash flood that has ripped through the border communities of Nepal and Tibet has heightened fears that the climate crisis is destabilising the geology of mountain and polar regions, threatening millions of people.

Satellite imagery suggests a glacier collapse high in the Himalayas was the primary cause of the deadly torrent of mud, water and ice that tore along the Bhotekoshi River on Wednesday. It swept away buildings and roads and left at least 360 dead and 1,400 missing.

events.summary:

Seven people charged with vandalising Donald Trump’s Turnberry golf course in Scotland have been accused of malicious damage “having a terrorist connection”.

When Lorde, Little Simz and Wet Leg stride on to stages in Bristol this weekend, they will not only be entertaining tens of thousands of festivalgoers but taking part in what is being billed as a world-first clean power project.

The two stages at Forwards festival on Clifton Down are being driven almost entirely by green power – a combination of hydrogen and mobile batteries charged with sustainable energy.

events.title: ‘Nature thrives when given a chance’: restored Cheshire wetland now a haven for rare grebe
events.summary:
Woolston Eyes in Warrington, a dumping ground for canal dredgings, has become best place in UK for black-necked grebe

A dumping ground for dredgings from the Manchester Ship Canal has become the best place in Britain for the rare and beautiful black-necked grebe, hosting 64% of Britain’s breeding population.

Since 2021, Woolston Eyes in Cheshire has been restored, extended and turned into a mosaic of freshwater pools, reedbeds, willow scrub and rough grassland, managed by the RSPB and Woolston Eyes Conservation Group.

events.title: Burnham announces crackdown on rogue bailiffs and ‘cowboy builders’
events.summary:

A clampdown on “rogue bailiffs” has been launched by Andy Burnham amid concerns that vulnerable people are being overcharged and face aggressive behaviour.

events.title: Federal judge again halts Trump’s executive order limiting mail voting in midterms

A federal judge on Thursday halted – at least for the moment – attempts to implement Donald Trump’s executive order limiting mail voting.

The president’s directive stalled for a second time about a week before the first mail ballots are due to be sent out for the rapidly approaching midterm elections. In the US district court, Judge Indira Talwani placed a 14-day hold on the government implementing the order in a case that could be headed back to the supreme court, which on Monday overturned an earlier ruling of hers that had blocked Trump’s order from taking effect.

On Wednesday, Trump officially signed a proclamation on Wednesday that suspends higher tariffs on 300,000 metric tons of foreign beef imports for 90 days. This comes after backlash to the proposal – designed to lower grocery costs for Americans in the run-up to the November midterms.

Several Republicans – in states with sizable cattle farming industries – have criticized the policy, saying it is a short term solution that will stymie ranchers’ ability to rebuild their herds.

Four leading livestock and agricultural organizations also wrote a letter to the president on Wednesday urging him to reverse course.

“Flooding the market with discounted foreign beef is not the way to rebuild the American cattle herd, strengthen food security, or lower grocery bills in a lasting way,” the groups wrote.

Donald Trump will begin his day in Washington, before traveling to Houston, Texas where he’ll headline a Republican National Commitee (RNC) fundraiser, and help boost Ken Paxton — the state’s attorney general and Republican nominee for Senate.

A reminder that Paxton beat long serving Senator John Cornyn in the GOP primary earlier this year after receiving Trump’s endorsement. Paxton is set to face Democratic state lawmaker James Talarico in November.

events.title: Harry and Meghan moving back to Britain: reports

events.title: Germany condemns Israeli minister's Gaza 'killings' remarks
events.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has denounced a call by Israel's far-right security minister to carry out "targeted killings" of Palestinians in Gaza. The outrage spans the entire political spectrum.

events.title: Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala collapses on pitch again

events.title: Germany news: Minister wants to help renters to install AC

events.title: Who really owns the Caspian Sea?
events.summary: Five countries border the Caspian Sea, but none owns a fixed share. A 2018 convention established rules for navigation, security and fishing while leaving some seabed borders unresolved.

events.title: Messi retirement hint highlights football era nearing an end
events.summary: Soon after propelling Argentina to a second consecutive World Cup final, Lionel Messi has cast some doubt on his future. While retirement doesn't seem imminent, it still beckons for him and Cristiano Ronaldo.

events.title: In drought-stricken France, tankers supply drinking water

events.title: Minors living alone on Ceuta's streets at risk of abuse
events.summary: Several thousand unaccompanied minors have gathered in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on the northern coast of Africa. Illness and abuse are rife, and the authorities admit they are overwhelmed.

events.title: Will Germany's drought push up food prices?
events.summary: Germany's main farmers' association has warned of a below-average harvest after drought and crops damaged by extreme heat. DW looks into what lower yields could mean for food prices and grocery bills.

events.title: Dressed for power: Giorgia Meloni and the language of fashion
events.summary: From Giorgia Meloni's shift from dark suits to pastels to Angela Merkel's signature jackets, politicians have long used clothing to shape how voters see them. In this day and age, power dressing has evolved.

events.title: How to grow food for more people in a hotter world

events.title: Belgium wildfire: Rains help High Fens containment efforts

events.title: How Germany's Hyrox became a global fitness craze

events.title: Ukraine, Russia trade strikes; Wildberries site hit again

events.title: Do not inhale! How wildfire smoke 'affects the whole body'

events.title: Norway wealth fund sounds alarm on AI stock market bubble

events.title: Wildfires: Belgium battles blaze, France's Lecornu jeered

events.title: Can the cool north handle a surge in climate tourism?
events.summary: With heat records continually being broken and southern summers getting hotter, travelers are heading north. Fragile ecosystems are paying the price.

events.title: Germany's AfD is labeled far right, populist or extremist

events.title: Fatty food raises risk of colorectal cancer

events.title: Germany news: Belgium blaze kept out of Germany for now

events.title: Why Kyiv keeps attacking Russian retail giant Wildberries

events.title: Afghan allies still waiting for the safety Germany promised

events.title: Germany: Evacuated villagers return after Eifel wildfire eases

events.title: Berlin's Russian House: A hub for propaganda and espionage?

events.title: Why women are breaking men's endurance records

events.title: Hunger stones: The history behind 'if you see me, weep'

events.title: Can a drug help prevent trauma? Study with mice suggests so

events.title: Can we go green without forever chemicals?

events.title: Eurovision bars countries at war from hosting

events.title: Mozart tribute ends on sour note after mass figurine theft

events.title: EU waste packaging rules: Why small businesses are worried
events.summary: The EU has introduced new rules targeting packaging waste and "forever chemicals." Although the changes will be phased in slowly, some small sellers have already paused shipments due to the additional red tape.

events.title: AI helping create popular mobile sports games
events.summary: After the World Cup and before the domestic season, many fans still crave more football. Amateur coders are helping to fill this gap.

events.title: Solar eclipse: What to look forward to

events.title: Making sense of Trump's executive order on US vaccinations

events.title: How one German city plans to challenge climate extremes

events.title: How the Rhine drought threatens Germany's economic recovery
events.summary: Germany's inland waterways still move around 5% of the nation's goods. With the Rhine at a critically low level, DW explores how the drought is hitting the economy where it hurts most.

events.title: UEFA, other football federations unite against Infantino

events.title: My sleep deprivation is your natural short sleep

events.title: South Sudan: How climate change can result in toxic water
events.summary: Years of flooding have resulted in disastrous water pollution in South Sudan's main oil region. As communities, scientists and health workers scramble for solutions, the long-term impacts of the crisis is yet to emerge.

events.title: Tennis star Sabalenka supports sport's new sex test policy
events.summary: The world number one women's tennis player supports the WTA's new sex testing rules. Others are more critical of the policy.

events.title: More cancer-prone? Why younger generations may be at risk
events.summary: Researchers are observing certain age-related types of cancer more frequently in younger people. A new study suggests this could be because younger generations are aging faster than their parents or grandparents.

events.title: Binging on cringe: It's as addictive as 'eating junk food'
events.summary: Flexing achievements? Cringe. Expressing genuine emotions? Cringe. You want to look away, but you can’t. Cringe. It's so addictive, people have built social media careers by monetizing other people's worst moments.

events.title: More women die in heatwaves, but biology 'isn't main cause'
events.summary: In country after country, more women are dying from the heat than men. But researchers say biology isn't the main reason. Age, working conditions, and unequal access to rest may drive the gap.

events.summary: From Greece to France, Europe is burning. But what's the real reason for the historic blazes ripping through the continent and why are they getting harder to stop?

events.title: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
events.summary: From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

events.title: Humanoid robots: Trump's latest China trade battle?
events.summary: The US has banned foreign-made humanoid robots, a market Chinese tech firms dominate. Although Washington cited national security risks, analysts think Donald Trump is buying time for US robot makers to catch up.

events.title: Eco wins: From death strip to nature haven and other green surprises
events.summary: A Cold War relic becomes a biodiversity haven, a Pokemon Go for trees and seagrass gets a second life. This week's eco wins come from some unexpected places.

events.summary: After regional football federations condemned FIFA plans for private investment, Carlos Cordeiro, senior advisor to FIFA President Gianni Infantino, tendered his resignation.

events.summary: Germany's state-mandated licensing agency, GEMA, says the verdict has "global significance," as Suno is also directed to pay yet-to-be-quantified damages.

events.title: BMW to Volkswagen: How deep is Germany's auto industry cull?
events.summary: BMW joins VW, Porsche and Mercedes-Benz in cutting thousands of jobs, as Chinese rivals erode their market share. DW recaps the major reforms German automakers are pursuing to safeguard their future.

events.title: Why Germany may stand up against FIFA's World Cup sell-off
events.summary: Leading figures in German football have lined up to criticize Gianni Infantino’s plans to sell a stake in the World Cup. Germany is showing signs that they may be ready to oppose Infantino's re-election.

events.title: 'Rienzi': Why this Wagner opera is so relevant today
events.summary: The opera sparked controversy long before its Bayreuth Festival premiere, and the debate hasn't died down since it came to the stage. Now, another controversy surrounds the new AI-generated Ring cycle.

events.title: 🔴 French Foreign Legion soldier kidnapped in Colombia
French Foreign Legion soldier kidnapped in Colombia
events.summary: Colombian military announced Thursday that a French-Colombian soldier from the French Foreign Legion was kidnapped in early August while travelling in the department of Narino. The kidnappers are believed to be members of the Estado Mayor Central, dissidents from the far-left FARC guerrilla group.

events.title: Champions League Draw: PSG to face Barcelona and Man City
events.summary: As part of the ongoing Champions League, two-time European champions PSG will host Barça and travel to England. Meanwhile, a host of meetings are set to take place including José Mourinho and his former clubs, Olivier Giroud with Arsenal and Yan Diomandé with Leipzig.

events.title: 🔴 Nepal-Tibet live: China halts rescue at disaster epicentre over flood risk
Nepal-Tibet live: Rescuers halt operations as lake overflows in disaster zone
events.summary: Rescue teams have suspended operations on Friday in the heart of the Tibetan disaster zone as authorities confirm that a lake formed by a mudslide on the China-Nepal border has burst, threatening further damage. The devastating flooding in Nepal and Tibet has claimed more than 400 lives and left hundreds missing, with ongoing conditions complicating rescue efforts. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

events.title: OpenAI, Anthropic join global call to strengthen cyber defences
events.summary: More than 100 organisations, including OpenAI and Anthropic, called governments and technology companies Thursday to strengthen cyber defences against increasingly sophisticated AI-powered attacks. The open letter warned of widespread threats in coming months as artificial intelligence models grow more capable.

events.title: Kherson residents urged to leave as Russian attacks threaten power and heating
events.summary: Regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin urged residents to leave the southern Ukrainian city of Kherson on Thursday as Russian strikes damaged a district heating plant and threatened prolonged power and heating outages.

events.title: US military faces ‘beyond critical’ shortage of Patriot missiles in Europe
events.summary: The US military is running critically low on Patriot missile interceptors in Europe as the war with Iran drains stocks, according to US and NATO officials. The shortfall is raising concerns about NATO’s ability to counter a potential Russian ballistic missile attack, though officials said no such assault is imminent.

events.title: Nigeria: the lucrative business of kidnappings
events.summary: In tonight's programme, we speak to a Lagos analyst behind a new report laying out the figures behind abductions. Also, Tanzania's ruling party kicks the vice-president out even after he announces his plans to step down next week. And finally in Senegal, the first African-manufactured generic drug to treat sickle cell disease is raising hopes of better treatment and reduced reliance on costly imported medicine.

events.title: Trump signs order to rename Lake Ontario to 'Lake America' as Carney pushes back
events.summary: US President Donald Trump on Thursday signed an executive order to update the name of Lake Ontario to "Lake America" in the country's geographic naming service. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney pushed back, citing the name's Indigenous origins, as the row between the neighbors roiled on.

events.title: French presidential candidates clash at first debate before upcoming elections
events.summary: Seven of France's leading candidates locked horns on Thursday in their first debate, eight months ahead of an increasingly tight and crowded election to succeed President Emmanuel Macron. The debate comes less than eight months ahead of the 2027 election to choose France's new leader, with centrist incumbent Macron having served the maximum two consecutive terms.

events.title: Red Cross mobilises in Nepal following natural disaster: 'Entire villages & communities washed out'
events.summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Tommaso Della Longa, Spokesperson for the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. The immediate challenge in Nepal is not only the scale of destruction, explains Della Longa, but the difficulty of reaching communities whose roads, bridges and communications have been swept away. Their priority remains search and rescue and the delivery of life-saving assistance, even as they begin preparing for longer-term recovery. Yet this is also a deeply human crisis for first responders: local Red Cross volunteers are supporting their own communities while some have themselves lost homes or relatives.

events.title: Why Trump wants H-1B skilled worker visas to cost employers more than $100,000
events.summary: US President Donald Trump is once again trying to impose a $100,000 fee on employers seeking to hire skilled temporary foreign workers through the H-1B visa programme. But while tech titans like Elon Musk have long championed the programme to draw top global talent to Silicon Valley, critics say the scheme aims to replace skilled US-born workers with cheaper – and more easily controlled – foreign guest workers.

events.title: Title holders PSG to face Barcelona and Man City as Champions League draw is made
events.summary: Two-time defending champions Paris Saint-Germain will host Manchester City and travel to Barcelona in the Champions League this season, after the 36-team draw was made Thursday. Real Madrid will face Inter Milan and ​Arsenal, among a host of mouth-watering clashes.

events.title: UEFA moves to file criminal complaint against Infantino over failed FIFA sell-off
events.summary: The Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) is preparing a criminal complaint in Swiss courts against FIFA president Gianni Infantino over his failed plan to sell a stake in World Cup revenues to investors, including Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital, for $4.2 billion, a price UEFA lawyers called a “fraudulently off-market price".

events.title: Pakistan: Protests continue in Azad Kashmir despite repression and internet blackout
events.summary: Harshly repressed protests that have shaken Pakistan-administered Kashmir since early June have continued through local legislative elections held in July and August. With internet access cut off and access by foreign media restricted, local residents are attempting to report on the situation on the ground.

events.title: Ratko Mladic, former general convicted of Bosnia genocide, dies
events.summary: Ratko ⁠Mladic, convicted of genocide for orchestrating ​the 1995 massacre of at least 8,000 Muslims in a U.N.-designated "safe area" of Bosnia, Europe's worst atrocity since World War Two, died on Thursday in U.N. custody. France 24's correspondent in Belgrade, Laurent Rouy, has the latest.

events.title: 'National treasure: If we could all be like Dolly, the world would be a much better place'
events.summary: As the world pays homage to the life and legacy of Dolly Parton, François Picard is pleased to welcome Nashville's Irene Kelley, Country musician and celebrated songwriter, alongside her daughter, Justyna Kelley, Country musician, songwriter, actress and producer. For the Kelley family, Dolly Parton’s significance lies in the extraordinary reach of her music, and even more in the way she turned intimate stories into something remarkably universal. Her songs were grounded in home and family, sharing life's immense struggles, while staying true to her values. The Kelleys see Parton as a national treasure who transcended generations, social class and the great political divide.

events.title: 'Great public test': French presidential hopefuls to face off at business summit
events.summary: Paris's Roland Garros tennis stadium will be the venue for a French presidential election warmup event on Thursday as seven from a crowded field of candidates will take to the stage at the Medef business leaders' annual end-of-summer seminar to defend their business and economic programmes. France 24's Charles Pellegrin reports.

events.title: Exclusive - French astronaut describes climate change as seen from space
events.summary: In her exclusive interview with FRANCE 24, French astronaut Sophie Adenot spoke from the International Space Station about the impacts of climate change and the changing face of Earth.

events.title: An 'icon' of contemporary art: A look back at the career of Yayoi Kusama
events.summary: Japan's Yayoi Kusama, one of the world's most celebrated contemporary artists, has died aged 97, her company said on Thursday, triggering tributes from around the world. Eve Jackson takes a look at how the woman dubbed the "polka dot queen" became an icon of the art world.

events.title: 'Extremely challenging' conditions hamper Nepal-Tibet flood rescue efforts
events.summary: With more than 1,000 people still missing after the devastating flash flood that hit Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday, international rescue teams are working to locate survivors. But, as France 24’s Navodita Kumari reports, they are facing “extremely challenging” conditions due to the weather, mountainous terrain and lack of infrastructure.

events.title: Why were so many Indian pilgrims in Tibet during the Himalayan mudslide disaster?
events.summary: Hundreds of Indian nationals are missing in Nepal and Tibet following a catastrophic Himalayan flood. They include several pilgrims doing the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, a mountain in Tibet that holds sacred significance for Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and the Tibetan Bon religion, explains FRANCE 24’s Leela Jacinto.

events.title: Ghana bars export of unrefined gold
events.summary: Ghana has announced a ban on the exporting of unrefined gold from the country.
